  "text": "Peter read the words again, hoping they might change. There is another island. Beneath them, Tomas had drawn a rough circle and written a name: Bellwether.

Mara leaned over his shoulder. “Is that where he went?”

Elian lowered herself into a chair. “He went looking for the first light. The one that burned before anyone built a lighthouse.”

She explained that the blue line on the maps traced a current hidden beneath the ordinary tides. It appeared only when the moon stood low, and it led east, past the reefs. Tomas had followed it years ago. He had promised to return before winter.

“Why didn’t you go after him?” Peter asked.

“Because someone had to keep this light burning.” Elian’s gaze shifted to the window. “And because the current demands a guide who has lost something.”

The compass shivered in Peter’s palm. Its needle no longer pointed north. It aimed through the wall, toward the black water.

Ada set the lantern beside it. “Then we leave tonight.”

Elian studied her, then Mara, before looking back at Peter. “At dawn, the passage will close. You have until then to decide what you’re willing to lose.”

A gust swept down from the ridge. The lamp guttered, and every shadow in the hut leaned toward the door.

From somewhere beyond the shore came three slow knocks.

Peter opened the letter’s folded edge. A final sentence waited there, written in a hand far shakier than Tomas’s: If you hear the bell, do not answer it.

Across the water, a bell rang once."
